Maria Chen: Heads-up — canary for `reranker-emb` (non-chat) spiked during the 09:12 run. 95th went from ~40ms to ~95ms intermittently.
Sachin Rao: ugh, saw that too. timestamps?
Maria Chen: thread start 2004501234. I pulled traces and perf counters. Initial hunch: continuous-batcher under low QPS is forming many tiny microbatches that nudge the kernel selector into an unfavourable path (fp32 fallback) because effective seq_len distribution looks different once prefix/KV cache logic runs.
Jorge Lopez: can you paste the batcher config and kernel selection logs? also any KV hit-rate metrics?
Maria Chen: KV hit-rate drops from 0.92->0.6 in the spike window. Config snippet below:
```
batcher:
  mode: continuous
  prefill_tokens_target: 128
  microfill_window_ms: 8
  allow_partial_queues: true
kernel_selector:
  prefer_quantized: auto
  seq_len_threshold: 64
```
Kyle Park: microfill_window_ms 8 is tiny. if many requests are short (10-20 tokens) the effective per-GPU occupancy is low and selector thinks quantized kernels aren't worth it.
Sachin Rao: what I worry about is KV cache thrash: low affinity between requests in the same batch -> more cache evictions -> longer recompute/loads -> kernel runtime increases. any evidence of KV miss inflation?
Maria Chen: yes, profile shows KV miss latency bumps and peak memory churn. I attached a flame graph link and the extractor logs (perf-bot uploaded to s3): s3://redwood-staging/perf/2004501234/reranker-canary/
perf-bot: upload complete — flame.svg, kv_traces.json, kernel_logs.txt
Jorge Lopez: quick idea — bias batch formation to group by (model_variant + kv-entry-hash mod N) or by prefix fingerprinting. That should improve cache affinity even if it slightly increases waiting time.
Kyle Park: Agree. We can also switch kernel_selector.prefer_quantized to `force_if_cache_hit>0.75` instead of `auto` so quantized kernel is chosen only when batch has good KV affinity.
Maria Chen: I ran a local sim where I forced grouping by prefix fingerprint for 2 minutes with synthetic load; 95th dropped back to 42ms and KV hit-rate improved to 0.89. downside: overall batching latency median increased by ~3ms.
Sachin Rao: acceptable trade for reranker SLAs. Can we add an adaptive rule: if per-batch kv_hit_estimate < 0.7 then increase prefill_tokens_target to aggregate more picks, else reduce to reduce tail?
Jorge Lopez: +1. also add metric: per-batch kernel_choice and kv_hit_estimate to the span so we can build a simple classifier later.
Maria Chen: putting a patch up: `eng-runtime:rb/emb-batch-affinity-200450` — it implements fingerprint grouping + kernel selector threshold + small telemetry tags. Will run a canary.
